clue.text: Ex-Soviet jet helping movement of refugees?

parts.note: the MiG is a Soviet-designed fighter jet
a helping is a portion, a ration

explanation.surface: A Soviet-era warplane apparently carrying food aid to displaced people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that refugees moving is one example of the broader sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Migration is mass relocation of people, of which a refugee exodus is a typical case.

clue.text: Greek character — adapt it to a name for variant

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: adapt means alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek letter assigned as a name to a new Covid variant.
explanation.walkthrough: Covid variants were named with Greek letters (Delta, Omicron), and Mu was one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutation is a changed form, the way a virus variant arises.

clue.text: Dancing alone, cabinet minister's out to enjoy a break from work

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the minister's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Michael Gove was a UK cabinet minister

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister caught dancing alone on his holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges the letters of alone. Michael Gove, then a cabinet minister, was filmed dancing alone in an Aberdeen nightclub in 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on leave is to take time off from one's job.

clue.text: A role could be found so Milan is on board

definitions.text: A role could be found so

parts.note: AC Milan is the Italian football club
a table is a board, as a board of food

explanation.surface: A part could be found for a Milanese actor joining the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: a role that could be acted. 'is on' stacks the pieces in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A role that is actable can be performed on stage, so a part found that way.

clue.text: One's informed of infectious contact that's encroached

parts.note: I'm is a short form of I am, one is
being pinged meant receiving the NHS Covid app alert after a contact

explanation.surface: Someone told by an app of a Covid contact that crept too close.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2021 the NHS Covid app 'pinged' people who had been near an infected person.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge is to intrude on or have an effect upon, so encroached is its past form.

clue.text: He's related expression of astonishment after North Shropshire's outcome

indicators.note: after says the exclamation is placed following the north and Shropshire pieces
outcome means the last letter of Shropshire

parts.note: phew is an exclamation of surprise or relief

explanation.surface: Someone's reaction to the North Shropshire by-election result, said to be relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets PHEW after N and E. In December 2021 the Lib Dems won the safe Tory seat of North Shropshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a male relative, a sibling's son.

clue.text: You heard? I invested in 'non-fungible token' that's no use

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the word, here a single letter

parts.note: you is pronounced like the letter U

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money goes into a venture

parts.note: NFT is the standard abbreviation for a non-fungible token, a digital collectible

explanation.surface: Someone asks if you know they put money into an NFT, which proved worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts I inside NFT, giving NFIT, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfit for purpose is useless; 'no use' works as an adjectival phrase.

clue.text: In revolt — Conservatives? Honest!

parts.note: up as in 'up in arms', rising in rebellion
the right is the conservative wing of politics

explanation.surface: Tory MPs rise up, insisting they are being truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and principled.

clue.text: Currents bearing off ice sheet and discontented walrus

indicators.note: off means a piece is taken away

parts.note: a floe is a sheet of floating ice
E, east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: discontented means with its contents removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A grumpy walrus drifting away on an ice floe.
explanation.definitionFit: Flows are streams or currents of water.

clue.text: Accepting job in government's first, relinquish second

indicators.note: relinquish means give up, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a task is a job

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of government

explanation.surface: Someone accepting a government post, then giving up their second job.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an offer is accepting it.

clue.text: French entirely blocking end of harbour to get fish

indicators.note: blocking means a letter sits inside and obstructs the other piece

parts.note: tout is French for all, entirely

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of harbour

explanation.surface: A French harbour is blocked off to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts R, the last letter of harbour, inside TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater game fish.

clue.text: Adult gets into origins of Peppa Pig with hesitation in front of function needing sheets of A4?

indicators.note: gets into means the letter goes inside the other piece
origins of takes the first letters of the two names

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
er is the sound of hesitation
to function is to work

explanation.surface: A children's cartoon pig hesitates before some task needing printer paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' puts A between the initials of Peppa Pig, a British children's cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperwork is documents and forms, typically printed on standard A4 office paper; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: In Afghanistan, a bilateral withdrawing sees new rulers

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the letters are read in reverse
In says the answer is concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A two-sided pullout from Afghanistan brings fresh rulers to power.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Afghanistan, a bilateral' backwards and the answer sits inside, as 'In' and 'withdrawing' signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taliban took power in Afghanistan in August 2021, months before this puzzle, so they were its recent governors.

clue.text: Singed fans after inserting end of flare? Creeps, entering with stealth

indicators.note: after inserting places the flare letter with the singed letters; here it lands at the front
end of picks the last letter of flare
to fan is to spread out, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone singed while fanning a flare tiptoes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' shuffles SINGED to DGESIN; the E from flare is nominally inserted but sits at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge in is to creep forward slowly and quietly into a place.

clue.text: Agreed test for where north and south should ideally end up?

definitions.text: for where north and south should ideally end up?

parts.note: on means agreed, as in 'you're on'
A level is the English school-leaving exam

explanation.surface: An exam, apparently, to measure the levelling-up of England's North and South.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are the exams English students take at 18. The surface alludes to the government's 'levelling up' agenda for the North-South divide.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal regions would be on a par, which is the political goal the clue imagines.

clue.text: 'Gathering', no longer unknown, turns into pitfall

indicators.note: turns means the remaining letters are read in reverse
no longer means that piece is dropped

parts.note: a party is a social gathering
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A get-together turns out to be a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer unknown' takes Y off PARTY, leaving PART, which 'turns' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap and a pitfall are both hidden dangers that catch the unwary.

clue.text: Combating bad stuff spreading online dealing with Covid?

definitions.meaning: ... in a literal sense, against the coronavirus

explanation.surface: A defence against online misinformation about the pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means against and a virus is malware or a germ, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Follow-up stage of project to throw out anything going north

parts.note: phase is a variant spelling of faze, to throw or disconcert

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means reading upwards, in reverse

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A plan to discard anything travelling north in the next part of a project.
explanation.walkthrough: PHASE, a variant of faze, means throw (as in unsettle); 'going north' reverses OWT.
explanation.definitionFit: Phase two is the second, following step of a planned programme.

clue.text: Body of water wanting European customs for meat products

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so this letter goes

parts.note: a sea is a body of water
usages are customs and habits

explanation.surface: Seaborne European customs checks holding up meat, a post-Brexit 'sausage war'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages are processed meat in a casing, one kind of meat product.

clue.text: One dropped by Starmer, character from Labour's centre-left? This one's not middle of the road!

definitions.text: This one's not middle of the road!

indicators.note: dropped by means the letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Keir Starmer, leader of the UK Labour Party
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: character from says a single letter is picked from Labour's
centre-left means the letter just left of the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A politics joke: Starmer drops someone from a centrist Labour faction that is not middle of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In LABOUR'S the centre is O; the letter left of it is B.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerb (US curb) edges a road, the opposite of its middle; also a cheeky jab at a centrist party.

clue.text: Corporation, second to supply power, is bust

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a large paunch

indicators.note: second to picks the second letter of supply

explanation.surface: A company goes bankrupt after a supply problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that goes belly up has failed, gone bust.

clue.text: Asian produce supply chain on the way regularly interrupted

indicators.note: supply as an adverb means flexibly, so these letters are bent into a new order
regularly interrupted keeps every other letter

explanation.surface: An Asian supply chain keeps getting disrupted in transit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as a noun but works as the adverb from supple. 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is a type of tea grown in China, a crop from Asia.

clue.text: Tend to turn nasty over river (that's almost all waste!)

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned bad, so the letters are scrambled
almost all means the last letter is lost

parts.note: urea is a waste product in urine

explanation.surface: Someone tending things that turn sour over a filthy river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets the anagram above the rest. The letters from UREA are also the Ure, a Yorkshire river, as the parenthesis remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture is to tend, nurse and bring up.

clue.text: Pumps empty, staple food being stockpiled — these are affected by inflation

indicators.note: being stockpiled means stored inside, so the food goes within the other letters
empty leaves only the outer letters

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: Fuel pumps run dry and staple foods are hoarded during a cost-of-living crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves the outer letters of Pumps and 'being stockpiled' stores the food inside. The 2021 UK fuel crisis saw panic buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices rise with inflation, the general increase in the cost of goods.

clue.text: Promote what'll get jabs in arms increasing

parts.note: hype is slang for a hypodermic needle or injection
up means going higher

explanation.surface: Booster shots going into arms are on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype up a product is to promote it with publicity.

clue.text: Leaders of Russia and Ukraine mobilise support around country

indicators.note: Leaders of takes the first letters of Russia and Ukraine

parts.note: to rally is to drum up backing

explanation.surface: The heads of Russia and Ukraine each rallying backing, a 2021 news picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rurally means in or around the countryside, country in its rural sense.

clue.text: Proof about 6th of January (and Capitol) receiving backing from Trump?

indicators.note: receiving means the joined letters take another letter in among them

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: 6th of takes the sixth letter of each named word
backing from picks the letter at the back of Trump

explanation.surface: Evidence about the 6 January Capitol riot, backed by Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth letters of January and Capitol are R and O; RE plus RO, 'receiving' the back letter of Trump, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction proof, a clean printing proof used for copying.

clue.text: Battles start to rage in G7 venue

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: St Ives in Cornwall hosted the G7 summit in 2021

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of rage

explanation.surface: Fights break out at a world leaders' summit.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a Cornish seaside town; 'in' puts the first letter of rage inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to struggle or fight hard.

clue.text: Climate summit in Glasgow forever held talks around new division of contributions

parts.note: COP26, the UN climate conference, was held in Glasgow in 2021
ay or aye is an old word for ever

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps around the other

parts.note: met means held a meeting

explanation.surface: Endless negotiations at the Glasgow climate summit over who pays what.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-payment is a shared contribution, the patient paying part and an insurer the rest.

clue.text: Disassemble oil installation — international organisation taking lead

indicators.note: taking lead says the second piece goes in front

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a rig is an oil platform

explanation.surface: A global body leads the dismantling of an oil platform.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig is to strip a ship or structure of its rigging, taking it apart.

clue.text: After setback, short-lived NI party leader to submit

indicators.note: a setback reads as set back, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Edwin Poots led Northern Ireland's DUP for only a few weeks in 2021

explanation.surface: A briefly serving Northern Irish leader gives in after a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop, or stoop to, is to bow down, yielding or lowering oneself.

clue.text: Trials of Conservative seen in clinches

indicators.note: seen in means these letters appear inside the other word

parts.note: presses as nouns are holds or embraces, like clinches
O is a short form of of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's legal ordeals, spotted in embraces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts OC inside PRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Processes are legal proceedings, so trials fit the plural noun sense.
